measured_suffix.section: grant/LSU completion, ID advance and RF next read-address control

source_chain.fact: The external data request is LSU data_req_out AND NOT PMP error; only permission-approved beats reach the SoC request queue.
CORE_REQ_REG instantiates u_data_request on the common system reset and ungated SoC clock; instruction fetch bypasses this particular module.
Current gnt_o is rst_ni && req_i && !valid_q; the request/PMP cone therefore remains in same-cycle grant feedback.
Normal aligned IDLE request with immediate grant stays IDLE; without grant it enters WAIT_GNT. Misaligned requests use WAIT_GNT_MIS / WAIT_RVALID_MIS.
lsu_req_done uses lsu_go/current FSM and next FSM equal IDLE. Delayed grant changes the cycle of ID/WB progression.
Writeback configuration stalls memory operations until outstanding ownership and LSU request completion allow ID progression; RAW and precise exception behavior must be retained.
ID and WB stalls gate id_in_ready_o.
id_in_ready_i gates IF-ID instruction/PC/flags capture together.
Read-register address is decoded from instruction bits. The physical raddr_a_i[2] endpoint is an IF-ID instruction-state alias, not an independently movable RF address pipeline.
LSU busy participates in core clock enable. A pulse generated on ungated SoC clock must be shown to reach a live actual-core sampling edge.

rejected_shortcuts: Do not remove req_i from the current combinational gnt_o: the existing payload/valid write conditions would capture a phantom request while idle.
Even if writes remain permission-qualified, ready-high grant changes the LSU/PMP-error completion and transaction ownership contract; it has not been proved safe.
Do not move only the physical RF address-labelled flop: the next instruction, PC and flags must stay aligned.
The existing generic soc_req_pipe proof explicitly permits request/payload changes under backpressure and asserts immediate grant. It cannot be reused as a proof of the narrower delayed-ack contract.

candidate_cycle_semantics.state: Empty queue and permission-approved held request: capture_intent=1, grant=0, downstream_req=0; edge captures payload and sets valid_q/ack_q.
ack_q=1 drives grant=1, downstream_req=0. Upstream request/payload must still match the tentative capture. At this edge ownership transfers; ack_q clears.
valid_q=1 and ack_q=0 expose stable payload downstream until downstream grant; no duplicate upstream acknowledgement.
Filtered req_i remains 0, so no tentative capture or ack. Actual LSU registered PMP-error handling remains unchanged and still needs whole-core verification.
Queue valid and ack clear asynchronously and endpoints reset together. Accepted or tentative undelivered tokens are cancelled. Withdrawal without common reset is outside the tested contract.

pytest.scope: 17 isolated candidate/receipt tests and 5 existing default request-pipe tests; Icarus runs candidate positive and six negative controls.

required_actual_core_proofs: Actual Ibex keeps each permission-approved request and its complete payload stable until delayed acknowledgement, except common reset.
The PMP decision cannot withdraw an already captured request before acknowledgement; denied beats never enter this queue.
LSU split-beat sequencing, first/second-beat errors, fault address and response ownership remain precise with delayed acknowledgement.
ID/WB hazards, retirement, branch/interrupt/exception ordering and core clock enable remain correct through the added cycle.
Common reset cancels queue, core and response endpoints together; no response arrives before its acknowledged request.
required_actual_core_scenarios: Prove permission-approved request and full 69-bit payload are held from tentative capture through delayed grant, including first-cycle to multicycle ID transition.
Prove no CSR/PMP update or fault decision can withdraw a tentatively captured beat; no denied beat is forwarded.

Exercise aligned byte/half/word reads and writes and every split offset with first/second PMP denial, bus error and overlapping grant/response; preserve first-failing address and exact response ownership.
Exercise load-use RAW, WB forwarding, adjacent stores, and branch stalled behind a store. Keep BranchTargetALU=1 and WritebackStage=1.
Exercise memory fault versus illegal instruction/IRQ/NMI/debug priorities and WFI/clock gating; prove ack is sampled while the actual core clock is active.
Reset before capture, during ack, while waiting for downstream grant and while waiting for response; common reset must include queue, core, fabric and response endpoint.

Use transaction/retirement refinement for latency changes, not fixed-cycle equivalence with unrelated interrupt timing assumptions. Run actual C10 boot/MBIST and precise exception programs before candidate adoption.
Only after actual-core protocol and architectural gates pass, synthesize an isolated source profile and run fresh setup/hold/electrical/route validation with original constraints and corners.
limitations: Finite directed actual candidate-module simulation is not a formal proof, actual LSU split-transfer proof, actual PMP proof, whole-core proof or boot regression.
The synthetic deny wire reproduces the source-level request mask only; real PMP/CSR and core state were not simulated.
The candidate adds one upstream acknowledgement and one downstream request cycle. Full instruction performance and interrupt-visible timing changes have not been measured.
The grant feedback cone is structurally registered, but RF/ALU/PMP capture paths remain; no timing improvement or timing closure is claimed.
No actual RTL, generated Ibex source, ALU candidate input, SDC, corners, PDK or full-chip state was edited. No full-chip native job was run or dispatched.

root_review.scope: Root independently rehashed all method/reference/source pins, prepared candidate and native outputs; repeated all focused tests including actual Icarus controls. Actual Ibex protocol remains unproved.
